pages.text: "Mom, the boat keeps creaking!" Bung sat straight up in bed. One lamp swayed under the awning. Ddori slept softly beside Bung.
"Can we sleep with the light on? I am too scared!" Bung pulled the blanket to the nose with both hands. Mom set down a bowl and sat by the bed.
Splish, splash! Water struck beneath the boat. Tap, tap! Something fell on the awning. Bung shut both eyes and hunched the shoulders high.
Mom lifted a little lamp. "Which sound scared you?" Bung pointed at the edge. "Creak, creak over there."
Mom lit the edge. Their mooring rope stretched taut to the post. "Our boat being tied there makes that sound." Another creak. Bung peered out.
Now she shone beneath the boat. Water splashed against it. The awning taps were night-dew drops. Laying Bung beside her, Mom sang softly, "Rocking, rocking, beside Mom!"
A big boat passed. Their boat rocked once. Bung drew sleeping Ddori's hand close. "Ddori is not scared at all."
Bung listened quietly. Creak was rope, splash was water, taps were dew. "Even in the dark, I know every sound!"
Bung lay close to Mom. "One, scared? Call Mom! Two, find the sound with a lamp! Three, stay close beside Mom!" She rested a hand on the blanket.
Mom drew Bung close and lowered the lamp. "Scary sounds are all right once you know them." Rock, rock! "Like a lullaby now. Rocking, rocking, beside Mom!" Bung's eyes closed.
